steps.name: Rename write path: store queries, rename_project use-case, submit handler, form live
steps.description: Replace the Store panic scaffolds project_rename_context / list_team_sibling_projects / update_project_name with the pinned SQL (component-boundaries.md). Implement foundry_services::projects::rename_project with the ordered-check contract (is_instance_admin -> context fetch -> trim -> no-op -> empty -> length (256 Unicode scalars) -> duplicate (case-insensitive sibling name match OR foundry_core::slugify(new) == sibling stored slug, self excluded by query) -> update) returning RenameOutcome::{Renamed,NoOp} / RenameProjectError. Replace the 501 submit_project_rename scaffold: Path<String> parsed to Uuid IN the handler (parse failure => uniform resource_not_found_page, no 400 oracle), Forbidden/NotFound => the same uniform 404, EmptyName/NameTooLong/DuplicateName => 422 bare ErrorFragment (marker project-rename-error) with the exact D4 copy, success and no-op => 200 bare instance_project_row.html fragment (same partial 01-01 landed, name updated, form re-mounted with _csrf via ensure_csrf_cookie, never extending base.html).
criteria: Submitting the rename form for 'Auth v2' with 'Identity Platform' returns a 200 bare row fragment showing the new name, and reloading the dashboard still shows 'Identity Platform' (persisted)
Submitting the unchanged current name returns the identical 200 row fragment with nothing written (quiet no-op: assert_project_delta proves the row byte-identical)
Signed-in non-admin and signed-out rename POSTs receive the uniform 404 byte-identical to a never-existed path, and the name is untouched on all read surfaces
A POST without the matching _csrf cookie/field pair is refused 403 by csrf_middleware before the handler runs; with the pair, the dashboard-name propagation leg passes
A garbled (non-uuid) project id and a well-formed unknown project id both receive the same uniform 404 — no 400-vs-404 or existence oracle
On every rename only projects.name changes: state-delta assertions on (name, slug, key_prefix, next_issue_number) fail closed on any identity-column drift

steps.name: Validation refusal arms: 422 with exact copy, boundary and uniqueness edges
steps.description: Un-pend the seven HTTP validation scenarios. The validation logic landed in 02-02; this step is assertion enablement plus closing any gap the arms expose: empty and whitespace-only names refused with 'Project name must not be empty'; a 300-character name refused with 'Project name must be at most 256 characters' while exactly 256 Unicode scalars is accepted (boundary both sides); within-team duplicates refused with 'Project name must be unique within the team' via all three D4 arms — exact sibling name, case-insensitive sibling name ('sandbox' vs 'Sandbox'), and slug collision (slugify('Sandbox!') == sibling stored slug 'sandbox'). Every refusal returns 422 + the bare project-rename-error fragment and leaves the persisted name unchanged on dashboard, board, and report. Harden the 02-02 property suites where these arms show holes (e.g. Unicode-scalar length counting, punctuation-only slug collisions).
criteria: Empty and whitespace-only submissions return 422 with exactly 'Project name must not be empty'; the project name is unchanged on every read surface
A 300-character name returns 422 with exactly 'Project name must be at most 256 characters'; a name of exactly 256 Unicode scalar values returns 200 and persists (both boundary sides pinned)
Exact-name, case-insensitive-name, and slugify-collision duplicates within the team all return 422 with exactly 'Project name must be unique within the team'; both projects keep their original names
All refusals are bare fragments (no base.html wrap) with marker project-rename-error; state-delta assertions confirm zero column drift on every refused rename

Property-based tests cover the length rule (chars vs bytes) and the uniqueness predicate across generated sibling sets including punctuation/case variants; owned scenarios un-pended and green; full suite, check-arch, fmt, clippy green
